rules.label: Full charity discount (0-250% FPL)
rules.quote: Federal Poverty Levels based on total household income, with sufficient supporting documentation provided by the patient, will have a 100% Charity discount processed.

rules.label: Uninsured discount
rules.quote: All Self-Pay patients, excluding elective cosmetic procedures and facility designated self-pay flat rate procedures , will receive discount similar to managed care, referred to as an "uninsured discount".

payment_plan.quote: You do not owe any more money after: You make 36 monthly payments, or You pay the full discounted amount in your payment plan.

notes: The policy mentions that some locations may have identified additional criteria for charity eligibility besides the Federal Poverty Levels (e.g., high medical costs, more lenient income levels).
Medicare accounts and non-Medicare inpatient accounts require supporting income verification documentation.

For Medicare beneficiaries, preferred income documentation is the most current year's Federal Tax Return; alternatives include state tax return, pay stubs, written documentation from income sources, bank statements for last three months, or current credit report.
The uninsured discount amount may vary by location based on state requirements, patient income levels, and local rates.
Patients confirmed to be uninsured are presented with an Uninsured Patient Information document at time of service and must sign and date it.
If a patient agrees to a payment plan, they may request to renegotiate it, including opportunity for a new financial assessment.
The hospital must inform patients of their rights in their preferred language.
Patients can refuse to let the hospital check for public program eligibility; if they refuse, they cannot sue the hospital for not giving discounts or not checking for helpful programs.
For insured patients, the hospital has 45 days to see if they can get help after the patient asks them.
After application, the hospital must tell the patient if they qualify within 21 days.
Patients may appeal a decision by asking in writing for a mistake check and filing the appeal within 30 days of the hospital's decision.
Before sending to collections, the biller must: explain services and fees in the patient's preferred language, bill insurance first (if applicable), and tell the patient in writing 30 days prior.
If bill is sent to collections without completing required steps, patient can file a complaint or take legal action.
Complaints may be filed with the hospital billing department, Health Care Policy and Financing, or via phone/email provided.
HealthONE Cares does not guarantee accuracy of pricing estimates on the website; final bills may differ substantially due to unforeseen complications, additional tests, non-hospital charges, etc.
r1_charity_full may leave out a condition: Policy requires sufficient supporting documentation for 100% charity discount.
